                                              • position
                                                1
                                                kind
                                                paragraphs
                                                paragraphs
                                                • To find your paid subscriptions, review every payment account across a full year where possible, then cross-check app-store subscriptions, payment-wallet agreements and receipts. Match each charge to a service and billing account. No single app-store list or statement search guarantees that you have found everything.
                                                • A charge can show the store or payment processor rather than the service you remember joining. An annual plan may appear only once. Treat the first pass as discovery, not an instruction to cancel every recurring payment. This guide helps build the list; ending an unwanted contract is a separate step.
                                                unchangedFromBaseline
                                                false
                                              • position
                                                2
                                                kind
                                                list
                                                heading
                                                Run a search with a visible boundary
                                                checkable
                                                true
                                                items
                                                • List the bank accounts, current and replaced cards, wallets and household billing accounts you are authorized to review. Mark any missing statement periods.
                                                • Review roughly twelve months where available. Look for repeating merchants, variable recurring amounts and single charges that may be annual renewals.
                                                • Check Apple subscriptions under each relevant Apple Account. On iPhone, Settings, your name, then Subscriptions is the current documented starting point.
                                                • Check Google Play subscriptions under the Google Account that made the purchase. Repeat for other accounts you use; a direct website subscription may not appear.
                                                • Review PayPal automatic payments and saved businesses, plus other payment services, phone bills or platform memberships you actually use.
                                                • Search your receipts and renewal messages for subscription, invoice, membership, trial, renewal and the unexplained statement wording.
                                                • Record the service, billing owner, actual amount and cycle, next known charge, and evidence. Mark uncertain matches unresolved rather than guessing.

                                                heading
                                                Find the billing owner before making changes
                                                paragraphs
                                                • [Apple's instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118428) explain where device subscriptions are managed and what to do when an item is missing. [Google Play's guidance](https://support.google.com/googleplay/answer/7018481) says to use the account holding the subscription and notes that uninstalling an app does not cancel it. A familiar app icon is therefore not the same as a billing record.
                                                • [PayPal's automatic-payment guide](https://www.paypal.com/us/cshelp/article/what-is-an-automatic-payment-and-how-do-i-update-or-cancel-one-help240) directs website users to Settings, Payments, then Subscriptions and saved businesses or Automatic Payments. A saved payment arrangement does not by itself prove that a monthly charge is active. Cross-check actual merchant terms and recent transactions.

                                                  • A $12 monthly platform charge
                                                  • Receipt names a video service and the owning account.
                                                  • Confirmed monthly subscription; $144 annual equivalent if unchanged.
                                                  • A $72 charge in March
                                                  • Email shows an annual renewal.

                                              • position
                                                8
                                                kind
                                                paragraphs
                                                heading
                                                Calculate the cost without hiding the next bill
                                                paragraphs
                                                • For a monthly plan, multiplying the current price by twelve gives an annual equivalent, not a guaranteed future bill total. For an annual plan, dividing by twelve helps comparison but does not change the fact that the whole renewal may be taken on one day. Keep the real cycle and next known charge beside any normalized amount.
                                                • Do not add a PayPal entry and the bank's matching PayPal debit as two subscriptions. Conversely, do not merge two identical charges until you have checked whether they belong to separate accounts or genuinely duplicate services. Shared households should compare their own authorized records rather than using another person's login without permission.
                                                unchangedFromBaseline
                                                false
                                              • position
                                                9
                                                kind
                                                paragraphs
                                                heading
                                                Unknown charges and decisions need different routes
                                                paragraphs
                                                • If you recognize the service, decide keep, review or cancel. Check storage, exports, household access and contract terms before ending something that holds essential data. Use [the cancellation guide](/guides/how-to-cancel-subscriptions) when you have identified the actual billing owner. Save confirmation and check subsequent statements.
                                                • If a charge may be unauthorized, contact the bank or card issuer promptly through a verified channel and follow its dispute process. Do not spend days attempting to decode a suspicious merchant while an account remains at risk. Avoid giving credentials to a search service simply because it promises to find every subscription.
                                                • Finish by recording what the sweep covered and what it could not cover. Missing older records, other household accounts and longer billing cycles remain limitations. Add a reminder before known renewals and update the list when a new plan starts; do not call it complete forever.
                                                unchangedFromBaseline
                                                false
                                              • position
                                                10
                                                kind
                                                faq
                                                items
                                                • q
                                                  Why is a subscription missing from my phone's list?
                                                  a
                                                  It may be billed directly by the provider, through another store, or under a different Apple or Google Account. Find the receipt and payment route rather than assuming it ended. Check only accounts you own or have permission to manage, and ask the relevant account holder to review their own list.
                                                • q
                                                  Will reviewing three months find annual plans?
                                                  a
                                                  It can miss them entirely. A longer statement history gives you a better chance of seeing annual charges, although even a year is not a guarantee. Search renewal emails and current account terms as well. Mark missing periods and unresolved leads so you know what remains outside the review.
                                                • q
                                                  Does cancelling an automatic payment cancel the service?
                                                  a
                                                  Not necessarily. Payment authorization and the underlying subscription contract are different things. Identify the billing owner and follow the service's cancellation procedure, then retain proof. If a charge is unauthorized, also contact your payment provider promptly rather than treating it only as an unwanted subscription.
                                                unchangedFromBaseline
                                                false

                                                      paragraphs
                                                      • A useful home maintenance schedule starts with the equipment you own, its instructions and the last confirmed service, not one universal list of replacement intervals. Use monthly owner checks, pre-season professional work and condition-based inspections as separate categories. Unknown history calls for a baseline assessment, not a guessed completion date.
                                                      • Perhaps you moved in with a folder of receipts that never mentions the water heater, or a calendar reminder says service the house without naming a system. Build one row per real task. This US-oriented guide is for scheduling and records, not instructions for gas, electrical, pressure-system or roof work.

                                                      paragraphs
                                                      heading
                                                      Why the task description matters as much as the date
                                                      paragraphs
                                                      • Inspecting is not replacing, testing is not repairing, and servicing one component does not necessarily complete every task on the system. A technician may check the heating equipment while an owner separately checks the filter. Write the work in the same terms as the manual or service report.
                                                      • [ENERGY STAR's checklist](https://www.energystar.gov/saveathome/heating-cooling/maintenance-checklist) distinguishes owner filter attention from contractor tasks. [EPA's septic guidance](https://www.epa.gov/septic/how-care-your-septic-system) shows why intervals depend on system type, household use and inspection findings. A general range is a prompt to establish your own schedule, not a promise that waiting to its far end is safe.
                                                      • Do not apply smoke-alarm replacement ages to every CO unit or connected detector system. Check each manufacturer's instructions. Likewise, do not assume a tankless heater uses the same maintenance procedure as a storage tank, or that every refrigerator has owner-accessible coils needing the same cleaning routine.

                                                      items
                                                      • List heating, cooling, hot water, alarms, drainage and the appliances actually present. Include specialist systems such as septic, a sump pump or chimney only if you have them.
                                                      • Find the brand, model and correct manual. Note whether access or the proposed procedure requires a qualified professional.
                                                      • Recover the last service report and record its actual scope. Mark dates estimated or unknown when the evidence is incomplete.
                                                      • Copy each required inspection, cleaning, test or replacement into a separate task with its source. Record any use-based or condition-based trigger.
                                                      • Put seasonal work before the local weather or usage period that matters. Do not assign the same month to every US climate.
                                                      • Book unknown or concerning systems for assessment, then use the findings to set the next action. Update the record when the work is confirmed complete.

                                                      paragraphs
                                                      • A new owner has a heating invoice from last autumn but no filter specification and no septic report. They record the heating visit as confirmed, identify the filter using the equipment instructions, and ask the septic provider for system records and a baseline inspection. They do not mark all three systems serviced on moving day.
                                                      • After the septic inspection, the professional's report identifies the type, condition and recommended follow-up. That information replaces the generic reminder. If an active leak or safety concern appears meanwhile, it becomes an immediate issue rather than waiting for the planned calendar slot.

                                                      Keep repairs outside the repeating checklist
                                                      paragraphs
                                                      • An abnormal smell, leaking tank, failed safety test or repeated electrical trip is not a routine reminder to snooze. Stop using unsafe equipment where appropriate and arrange the relevant urgent help. If there is immediate danger, move to safety and contact emergency services. Do not open live panels or improvise gas or pressure-system maintenance.
                                                      • For each completed job, save the date, person or company, findings, work performed and next recommendation. [The maintenance-log guide](/guides/home-maintenance-log-template) covers that record. A schedule says what should happen; the log proves what actually happened. If you rent, record reports to the landlord and agreed responsibilities rather than taking on unapproved repairs.

                                                      • q
                                                        Should every home system be serviced annually?
                                                        a
                                                        No. Different systems and tasks have different intervals, and some checks are seasonal or condition-based. Heating and cooling often have pre-season professional checks, while filters and alarms need separate owner attention. Identify the exact equipment and procedure before copying an annual reminder across the house.
                                                      • q
                                                        What if I cannot find the last service date?
                                                        a
                                                        Mark it unknown and gather the manual, model details and any available invoices. Arrange a suitable baseline assessment where needed instead of assuming the system was serviced when you moved in. Unknown history does not mean every maintenance procedure is safe to perform yourself immediately.
                                                      • q
                                                        Can I use a generic interval until I find the manual?
                                                        a
                                                        Use it only as a reminder to verify or inspect, not as proof that the system is within a safe service window. Equipment type, age, usage and local conditions can change the answer. Visible faults or failed safety tests need action regardless of the generic calendar.

                                                        • position
                                                          1
                                                          kind
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          • When you buy an appliance, record its exact model and serial number, seller and purchase evidence, installation date, written warranty terms and the location of its manual. Photograph the identification label safely and type the identifiers into a searchable note. Do not guess a warranty end date from the brand alone.
                                                          • Delivery day can leave you with packaging in the hallway and a receipt buried in email. You do not have to build a whole home inventory now. Make one record for the new item while you can still connect the paperwork to the actual machine. This guide concerns records, not installation or repair instructions.
                                                          unchangedFromBaseline
                                                          false

                                                          kind
                                                          list
                                                          heading
                                                          Capture the details that are difficult to recover later
                                                          checkable
                                                          true
                                                          items
                                                          • Name the appliance and location so another person can distinguish it from similar units. Copy the exact model including suffixes, not only the marketing name.
                                                          • Photograph the serial label where safely accessible, then transcribe it carefully and check letters against digits. Do not move heavy equipment or remove service covers just for a photo.
                                                          • Save the receipt or invoice, seller, order reference, purchase date and price. Keep delivery and installation evidence separately if those dates differ.
                                                          • Save the written warranty and identify who provides it, when coverage starts, what is covered and how claims are made. Mark uncertain dates for confirmation.
                                                          • Keep the correct owner manual and any installer documentation, commissioning record or required certificate. Link files to this appliance rather than leaving them in a general downloads folder.
                                                          • Record any model-specific consumable or accessory specification you actually need, such as the approved filter part number. Verify it in the correct manual before buying spares.
                                                          • Check the official recall information for the exact affected model or serial range and follow any applicable safety instruction.

                                                          heading
                                                          Model and serial answer different questions
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          • The model identifies a product configuration; the serial identifies the particular unit. Repair, warranty or recall enquiries can need both. [GE's official locator](https://www.geappliances.com/ge/find-model-serial-number/) provides product-specific help finding them. Locations differ, so do not assume every refrigerator or washer uses the same label position.
                                                          • A photograph is useful only if it is readable. Check focus and glare before closing the door or discarding packaging. A photo can preserve a transcription error just as easily as a typed note if you capture the wrong sticker. Keep the full label and the text together, without posting serial details publicly.

                                                          paragraphs
                                                          heading
                                                          Keep the terms, not just a single expiry date
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          • A warranty may distinguish parts, labor, certain components, shipping and different coverage periods. A paid service contract is also not necessarily the same thing as the included warranty. The [FTC warranty guide](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/warranties) explains why the written conditions and claims route matter. This page does not decide whether an extra plan is worth buying.
                                                          • Check registration instructions in the actual terms and applicable law. Do not assume either that registration always creates coverage or that it never affects an additional benefit. Save any registration confirmation, but do not confuse it with proof of purchase or a guarantee that every future fault will be covered.
                                                          unchangedFromBaseline
                                                          false
                                                        • position
                                                          9
                                                          kind
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          heading
                                                          Recall checks are independent of warranty dates
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          • Use the [CPSC recall and safety-warning listings](https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls) in the US and compare the identifiers specified in any relevant notice. A similar appearance is not enough to establish a match. A recall remedy can have its own process; follow the exact notice rather than applying a general repair idea.
                                                          • Registration or official alerts can help you hear about later notices, but a general alert is not a substitute for checking whether your unit falls in an affected range. If a notice says to stop use, do not wait for the next maintenance reminder or assume an expired warranty makes the notice irrelevant.
                                                          unchangedFromBaseline
                                                          false
                                                        • position
                                                          10
                                                          kind
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          heading
                                                          If the appliance came with the house
                                                          paragraphs
                                                          • Record purchase date and warranty status as unknown unless you have evidence. Ask the previous owner, installer or manufacturer what can be recovered. Do not assign an invented age from its appearance or promise transferable warranty coverage. Use [the model-number guide](/guides/how-to-find-the-model-number-on-any-appliance) for identification before contacting support.
                                                          • After any repair, add the date, fault reported, work completed, provider and evidence. When an item is sold, removed or replaced, mark that change so a future owner does not order parts for the old machine. Share useful manuals and records while removing payment details and other personal information that do not belong in the handover.

                                                          items
                                                          • q
                                                            Is a receipt enough for an appliance record?
                                                            a
                                                            It proves some purchase details but may not identify the exact installed unit or explain coverage conditions. Keep it with the model, serial, installation evidence and written warranty. That combination lets you answer a support enquiry without trying to reconstruct which machine an old invoice described.
                                                          • q
                                                            Should I write one warranty end date?
                                                            a
                                                            Only when the written terms support that date and scope. Some coverage periods differ by component or parts versus labor, and start dates can depend on the terms. Record the document and any uncertainty. A clear pending question is better than a confident but invented expiry date.
                                                          • q
                                                            What if I cannot reach the identification label safely?
                                                            a
                                                            Do not pull out a heavy or connected appliance, climb onto it or remove service covers just to finish the record. Check the manual, packaging, delivery paperwork or manufacturer locator first. Ask an installer or technician to capture the label during appropriate safe access if necessary.

                                                              • position
                                                                1
                                                                kind
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                • To find a will after someone dies in the US, check the person's lawful paper storage, ask the drafting attorney or successor firm, and contact the probate court serving their last residence. Ask about a safe-deposit box through the bank's deceased-customer process. Keep a search record, preserve every version and check local deposit requirements promptly.
                                                                • You may have heard only that the will is with a lawyer, without knowing which lawyer or whether the document at home is the signed original. Treat that as a lead rather than an answer. This guide concerns finding and preserving evidence; it cannot determine whether a document is valid or which state's law governs a disputed estate.
                                                                unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                false
                                                              • position
                                                                2
                                                                kind
                                                                list
                                                                heading
                                                                Search without changing the evidence
                                                                checkable
                                                                true
                                                                items
                                                                • Ask the person coordinating the estate whether an original, copy, later amendment or attorney contact is already known. Agree who will record the search.
                                                                • Check accessible files, document boxes and other places you are entitled to search. Keep papers together and note where each document was found.
                                                                • Contact the drafting attorney or firm through independently verified details. Ask whether it holds an original, only a copy, or a record of transfer to another custodian.
                                                                • If a lawyer retired or a firm closed, ask about the successor practice or file custodian. A local bar association may help identify the correct enquiry route.
                                                                • Ask the probate clerk whether a will or estate case has already been lodged, and whether local law provides for depositing wills before death. No result is not proof that no will exists.
                                                                • If a bank box or locked storage is involved, ask for the specific lawful access procedure. Do not assume possession of a key grants access to the contents.
                                                                • Photograph or copy found documents for reference while preserving originals intact. Record custody and ask the court about the required next step.

                                                                5

                                                                paragraphs
                                                                heading
                                                                Ask about the deadline early, not after the whole search
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                • Finding every possible version can take time, but a custodian's duty to deposit an original may already have started. [Florida section 732.901](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0700-0799/0732/Sections/0732.901.html) requires the custodian to deposit the will with the court having venue within ten days after receiving information of the death. That is a Florida example, not a national deadline.
                                                                • California court guidance describes a different deadline: thirty days after learning of the death for delivering the original, subject to the applicable rules. Ask the relevant clerk for current instructions, required accompanying information and whether there are related copy-delivery duties. Depositing a will and applying to administer an estate are separate acts. Do not postpone the first because you are not ready for the second.

                                                                7

                                                                paragraphs
                                                                heading
                                                                Invented example: a copy and a later document
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                • A niece finds a photocopy dated several years earlier. The firm named on it says the original was returned to the client. She records that answer and asks the bank about lawful access to a box mentioned in correspondence. A later signed document is eventually found through the permitted process.
                                                                • She keeps both versions, the firm's response and the discovery dates. She does not destroy the earlier copy or decide that a later date alone proves the newer paper governs. A probate attorney reviews the documents, including whether an amendment changes only part of an earlier will. The example is about evidence handling, not a rule for choosing between wills.

                                                              • position
                                                                9
                                                                kind
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                heading
                                                                A will does not appoint you by discovery
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                • Read who is nominated, but do not assume that person can immediately withdraw money or sell property. [New York Courts explains fiduciary appointment](https://www.nycourts.gov/help/when-someone-dies/fiduciary-estate): appointment and duties are handled through the court process there. Your state may have a different procedure or a small-estate alternative. Finding the will does not make the finder the representative.
                                                                • Do not use a deceased person's login or power-of-attorney paperwork as a shortcut to search private accounts. Ask the institution and an estate adviser what access is permitted after death. Beneficiary designations, jointly owned property and trusts may follow routes outside the will, so the will itself is not necessarily an inventory of everything the person owned.

                                                              • position
                                                                11
                                                                kind
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                heading
                                                                If no original appears, or relatives disagree
                                                                paragraphs
                                                                • Keep the search log and seek advice about the next process. A missing original does not automatically mean there was never a will, and a photocopy is not automatically useless. Local evidence rules determine what can be proved. Similarly, do not assume an informal handwritten note is either valid or invalid without advice.
                                                                • Escalate promptly if someone refuses to produce a known document, pages appear missing or altered, property is being distributed, or there are competing claims about capacity or pressure. Do not confront a disputed document by writing on it or destroying another version. Preserve what you have and ask about protective steps.
                                                                • If the estate proceeds without a valid will, the applicable intestacy and appointment rules determine the route. They are not a family vote about what seems fair. Use [the US executor guide](/guides/named-executor-what-you-agreed-to) to understand the distinction between locating documents and accepting estate administration.
                                                                unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                false
                                                              • position
                                                                12
                                                                kind
                                                                faq
                                                                items
                                                                • q
                                                                  Can I search for the will online?
                                                                  a
                                                                  You can check the relevant court's official records and any locally available deposit or registry process, but no universal US website contains every private will. A negative search does not prove absence. Combine court enquiries with the home-paperwork and attorney-custodian search, keeping dates and responses.
                                                                • q
                                                                  Does the newest document always win?
                                                                  a
                                                                  Not simply because its date is later. Validity, amendments, revocation and the interaction between documents can matter. Preserve all versions and ask a qualified estate attorney to assess them. Do not tear up an older will or mark it cancelled based only on your own reading.
                                                                • q
                                                                  Can I open a bank box if I have its key?
                                                                  a
                                                                  A key is not a universal authorization. The bank and applicable state law determine who can access a deceased customer's box, what evidence is required and what may be removed. Ask specifically about a will-search procedure and keep any bank record of the access and document handling.

                                                                  • position
                                                                    1
                                                                    kind
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    • Being named executor in a US will nominates you for estate administration; it does not automatically prove you have authority to transact. First decide whether you can serve, locate the will, identify the applicable probate or alternative process, and protect urgent interests without distributing property. If appointed, you manage estate duties rather than simply hand out inheritances.
                                                                    • Your name may appear in a document written years ago, before the family circumstances or your own capacity changed. You can ask what the job involves before promising to do it. This is a first-decision guide, not a state-specific probate manual, tax opinion or instruction to take actions beyond your authority.
                                                                    unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                    false
                                                                  • position
                                                                    2
                                                                    kind
                                                                    list
                                                                    heading
                                                                    Before accepting transactions as routine
                                                                    checkable
                                                                    true
                                                                    items
                                                                    • Locate the original will and any amendments. Identify co-nominees and alternates without deciding contested validity yourself.
                                                                    • Ask the relevant court about will-deposit duties, the appointment process, any small-estate alternative, required notices and urgent deadlines.
                                                                    • If unsure about serving, ask about declining before undertaking substantive administration. Explain exactly what you have already done rather than assuming one call either commits you or means nothing.
                                                                    • List immediate care, security, insurance or business-continuity concerns and ask who may lawfully handle them pending appointment.
                                                                    • Gather an initial map of assets, debts and ownership. Separate possible estate assets from joint, beneficiary-designated or trust assets needing another route.
                                                                    • Keep a dated decision and expense record from the start. Do not mix estate receipts with your own spending or make informal promises of distributions.

                                                                    5
                                                                    kind
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    heading
                                                                    Authority comes before ordinary estate transactions
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    • In New York, [the court appoints the fiduciary](https://www.nycourts.gov/help/when-someone-dies/fiduciary-estate). The court document and permitted powers matter when dealing with institutions. Other states use their own processes and terminology. Ask which evidence each institution needs rather than presenting the will as a universal withdrawal authorization.
                                                                    • A power of attorney used during life is not a substitute for the post-death estate process. Do not impersonate the deceased person online, transfer a balance into your own account, or sign a sale because a family member says the will makes it yours anyway. Ask about necessary temporary authority if a genuine urgent transaction cannot wait.

                                                                      • Inventory, ownership evidence and secure records.

                                                                      • Supported date-of-death values and specialist advice where needed.

                                                                      • A schedule of notices, returns, liabilities and reserves.

                                                                      • Distribute and close
                                                                      • Approved accounting, receipts and closure evidence.
                                                                      • Have claims, taxes, restrictions and required approvals been resolved?

                                                                  • position
                                                                    7
                                                                    kind
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    heading
                                                                    Invented example: a house, an account and an old pension
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    • A nominated executor finds a house with a mortgage, one sole-name bank account and a retirement statement naming an administrator. They record these as leads. They do not assume the pension is part of the probate estate, or promise the house to one sibling before checking ownership and the will.
                                                                    • They ask the court about appointment, the bank about required documents and the plan administrator about the benefit-claim route. The first useful output is a verified map and next-action list, not a total inheritance figure. If a mortgage or insurer needs immediate contact, they gather instructions and document who has authority for the action requested.

                                                                  • position
                                                                    9
                                                                    kind
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    heading
                                                                    Separate the deceased person's tax from estate administration
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    • The [IRS administrator guidance](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/responsibilities-of-an-estate-administrator) distinguishes obligations involving the deceased person and the estate. Ask a qualified tax adviser which federal and state filings are required, who signs them and when. Do not assume that a small estate means no final income-tax work, or confuse estate income tax with estate transfer tax.
                                                                    • Where an estate identification number is needed, use the [official IRS EIN route](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/get-an-employer-identification-number), not an unsolicited paid intermediary. An EIN is not proof of court appointment. Ask the bank what authority and identification it requires before opening an estate account; do not create accounts merely to feel the process has started.
                                                                    unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                    false
                                                                  • position
                                                                    10
                                                                    kind
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    heading
                                                                    Personal liability is about duties, not inheriting every debt
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    • The [FTC explains that estate debts are generally paid from estate assets](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/debts-and-deceased-relatives), with exceptions affecting some personal obligations. An estate representative can also create problems by mishandling legal duties. Do not pay creditors in the order they call or distribute funds on the assumption that later claims can simply be ignored.
                                                                    • If liabilities may exceed assets, stop before paying or distributing and seek probate advice about priorities. The same applies to disputed wills, taxes you cannot assess, a business, foreign property, missing funds or a sale to yourself or another relative. A lawyer's fees, compensation and reimbursement arrangements should be agreed and checked against the will, law and any required approval; estate payment is not an unlimited guarantee.
                                                                    unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                    false

                                                                    • situation

                                                                      I am nominated in the will and have not established transaction authority. Which steps preserve the estate, what appointment route applies, and what deadlines need attention now?
                                                                    • situation

                                                                  • position
                                                                    12
                                                                    kind
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    heading
                                                                    Give the family process updates, not premature promises
                                                                    paragraphs
                                                                    • Record receipts, values, provider responses and the basis for decisions. Agree a practical update channel so beneficiaries know what is confirmed and what remains unresolved. Being both a beneficiary and nominated executor does not remove the need to handle competing interests carefully.
                                                                    • Do not promise completion in a set number of weeks. Court processing, claims, tax questions, sales and disputes can each control the pace. Track actual milestones and ask for help with a specific blocked decision. Hiring help does not automatically transfer all your responsibilities; clarify who is doing what in writing.
                                                                    unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                    false
                                                                  • position
                                                                    13
                                                                    kind
                                                                    faq
                                                                    items
                                                                    • q
                                                                      Do I have to serve because the will names me?
                                                                      a
                                                                      Nomination does not mean you must silently take the job on. Ask the relevant court or probate attorney how to decline and explain anything you have already done. If you have been appointed, stepping down requires the proper release or replacement process; do not simply stop responding or hand the file to a relative.
                                                                    • q
                                                                      Can I distribute money once I find the will?
                                                                      a
                                                                      Not simply because the will has been found. Authority, ownership, creditor procedures, tax obligations and any required approval must be checked. A distribution that seems obvious to the family can still be premature. Preserve the money and get advice before paying inheritances or moving estate funds into personal accounts.
                                                                    • q
                                                                      Does the executor personally pay the estate's debts?
                                                                      a
                                                                      Not automatically from personal funds, but personal obligations and mistakes in administration can change the position. Ask about responsibility before making promises or payments. If the estate may be insolvent, get advice about claim priorities and required procedure instead of paying whichever creditor applies the most pressure.

                                                                        • If you are named executor in a UK will, first identify the applicable national estate process, decide whether you can act and preserve the information needed to administer the estate. Do not assume one UK-wide form or that finding your name lets you complete every transaction. Probate in England and Wales, Scottish confirmation and Northern Ireland procedures differ.
                                                                        • You may have agreed years earlier without seeing the eventual property, debts or family situation. Before promising beneficiaries a payment date, establish what must be done and whether you need professional help. This is general administration guidance, not legal advice or a complete procedure for every UK estate.
                                                                        unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                        false
                                                                      • position
                                                                        2
                                                                        kind
                                                                        list
                                                                        heading
                                                                        Before substantive administration
                                                                        checkable
                                                                        true
                                                                        items
                                                                        • Find the original will and amendments, identify every named executor and check any substitute appointment. Preserve documents rather than annotating or dividing them.
                                                                        • Establish the relevant jurisdiction and ask about cross-border property or domicile uncertainty. Do not select a court only because it is nearest to you.
                                                                        • List urgent care, security, insurance and business issues. Ask who may handle them while authority and grant requirements are being established.
                                                                        • If you do not want to act, get advice about your options before taking substantive steps. Disclose anything already done; do not guess whether it counts as administration.
                                                                        • Create an initial asset, ownership and liability list. Note unknowns instead of assuming every pension, policy and joint account falls into the distributable estate.
                                                                        • Keep correspondence, expenses and decisions dated. Do not mix funds or promise an inheritance before claims, tax and authority questions are understood.

                                                                        heading
                                                                        Use the correct official route
                                                                        columns
                                                                        • Jurisdiction
                                                                        • Official starting point
                                                                        • What not to assume
                                                                        rows
                                                                          • England and Wales
                                                                          • GOV.UK applying for probate and estate-administration guidance.
                                                                          • That every estate needs a grant, or that renunciation and power reserved are the same.
                                                                          • Scotland
                                                                          • Scottish Courts guidance on dealing with a deceased estate and confirmation.
                                                                          • That England/Wales probate forms or inheritance rules apply.

                                                                      • position
                                                                        6
                                                                        kind
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        heading
                                                                        Deciding not to act needs the right procedure
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        • For England and Wales, [GOV.UK explains options where there is a will](https://www.gov.uk/applying-for-probate/if-theres-a-will). Where more than one executor is named, power reserved can retain the ability to apply later; renunciation gives up the right to apply through its stated process. These are different decisions with different effects. Check the current form and conditions rather than copying a letter found online.
                                                                        • [NI Direct](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/probate) describes its own reserved-power and renunciation position. In Scotland, ask a Scottish solicitor or the relevant court about your circumstances rather than using an England/Wales form. If you have already started dealing with the estate or a grant has issued, get advice before assuming you can simply withdraw.
                                                                        • Helping with immediate funeral or safety arrangements is not a reason to make your own legal judgment about whether you have committed to the full role. Describe the exact acts to an adviser. If another executor will act, agree who will preserve records and communicate while the formal position is settled.
                                                                        unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                        false
                                                                      • position
                                                                        7
                                                                        kind
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        heading
                                                                        Invented example: two executors with different capacity
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        • A will names two siblings. One can manage paperwork now; the other is caring for a child and cannot take on routine administration. They identify the England/Wales route and ask about applying with power reserved to the second executor rather than describing both siblings as having renounced.
                                                                        • Before choosing, they check whether either has already taken substantive steps and what notices or written communication are needed. If the same family were dealing with a Scottish estate, they would not copy this option automatically. The example demonstrates a question to ask, not a recommendation for every joint appointment.

                                                                        9
                                                                        kind
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        heading
                                                                        The role lasts beyond obtaining a grant
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        • [GOV.UK's estate overview](https://www.gov.uk/probate-estate) describes responsibility for estate assets during administration. The work can include identifying property, establishing values and ownership, collecting assets through the appropriate process, dealing with liabilities and tax, then distributing and accounting. Obtaining a grant is a milestone, not proof the estate is ready to pay out.
                                                                        • [Scottish Courts' confirmation guide](https://www.scotcourts.gov.uk/taking-action/dealing-with-a-deceaseds-estate-in-scotland/guide-to-dealing-with-a-deceaseds-estate-in-scotland/) explains the estate inventory in its own system. Do not reuse an informal family estimate where the process requires a supported value. Seek suitable valuation or tax advice for property, a business or uncertain ownership.
                                                                        unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                        false
                                                                      • position
                                                                        10
                                                                        kind
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        heading
                                                                        Separate debts, tax and beneficiaries' expectations
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        • Record known bills, possible claims and the tax questions requiring professional review. Do not pay creditors simply in order of arrival or distribute the apparent bank balance without reserves and the required checks. If the estate may be insolvent, stop and ask about the applicable priority rules. A friendly family agreement cannot necessarily remove another claimant's rights.
                                                                        • The deceased person's final tax position and income arising during administration can be different issues. Ask which information HMRC and the relevant estate process require for the date of death and estate circumstances. This guide deliberately does not supply a universal tax threshold, clearance period or deadline.
                                                                        • Ask a solicitor about creditor notices and any applicable protective process before relying on them. Such notices are not a universal UK immunity from every claim. Disputed entitlement, dependants' claims, foreign assets, missing funds, capacity concerns or plans for an executor to buy estate property need particular care.
                                                                        unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                        false

                                                                        11
                                                                        kind
                                                                        scripts
                                                                        heading
                                                                        Ask before taking the next step
                                                                        items
                                                                        • situation
                                                                          To an adviser
                                                                          line
                                                                          I am named executor, the estate appears to involve [assets and debts], and these actions have already happened: [facts]. Which national process applies, can I step aside, and what must be protected now?
                                                                        • situation
                                                                          To beneficiaries
                                                                          line
                                                                          I am confirming authority, ownership and the estate's liabilities. I cannot promise a distribution date yet. I will update you when [specific information] is confirmed.
                                                                        unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                        false
                                                                      • position
                                                                        12
                                                                        kind
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        heading
                                                                        Agree help, costs and a manageable record
                                                                        paragraphs
                                                                        • If using a professional, ask who is the client, what work is included, how fees are calculated, who authorizes extra work and what you remain responsible for. Do not assume every proposed expense can be reimbursed from the estate without question. Keep the engagement and supporting invoices.
                                                                        • Record the date, transaction, amount, evidence and reason for every estate payment or receipt. Keep an issues list with an owner and next action rather than relying on messages between relatives. Beneficiaries need accurate progress information, but a fixed completion promise is unreliable where sales, tax, claims or disputes control the timetable.
                                                                        • For registration and immediate notifications, use [the UK first-steps guide](/guides/what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies-uk). For this decision, the main outcome is simpler: you know the jurisdiction, your intended role, the evidence of authority needed and which action cannot safely wait.
                                                                        unchangedFromBaseline
                                                                        false
                                                                      • position
                                                                        13
                                                                        kind
                                                                        faq
                                                                        items
                                                                        • q
                                                                          Does agreeing during their lifetime mean I must act?
                                                                          a
                                                                          Not necessarily, but you should establish the correct national procedure and disclose what you have already done. Options and consequences differ between declining before acting and leaving after substantive administration or a grant. Get advice before signing a renunciation or assuming silence transfers the role to someone else.
                                                                        • q
                                                                          Is power reserved the same as renunciation?
                                                                          a
                                                                          No. In England and Wales, power reserved can preserve the right to apply later where other executors are applying, while renunciation gives up that right through the stated process. Northern Ireland has its own position and Scotland uses a different system. Verify the applicable route before choosing forms.
                                                                        • q
                                                                          Can I pay beneficiaries once probate is granted?
                                                                          a
                                                                          A grant does not itself resolve debts, tax, disputed ownership or other claims. Check the estate's liabilities, required procedures and reserves before distributing. If there is uncertainty or pressure to pay early, seek advice and explain which issue is outstanding rather than treating the grant date as an automatic payout deadline.

                                                                              • position
                                                                                1
                                                                                kind
                                                                                paragraphs
                                                                                paragraphs
                                                                                • An if-something-happens-to-me file is a map of important people, documents, accounts and household responsibilities. It tells an appropriate person what exists, where to look and whom to call. It does not give that person legal authority, change who inherits, or replace a will, power of attorney or health-care directive.
                                                                                • The question is smaller than sorting your entire life: if you could not explain things tomorrow, where would someone start? Not every account number. Not every password. Just enough accurate directions to stop the first person helping you from searching every drawer.
                                                                                • This guide is for adults preparing practical information for illness, incapacity or death. Legal authority, privacy and document requirements depend on the situation and location. Ask a qualified professional about the documents you need rather than treating this folder as a legal plan.

                                                                                false

                                                                                heading
                                                                                Make a useful first page
                                                                                checkable
                                                                                true
                                                                                items
                                                                                • Choose who should know that the file exists, and ask whether they are willing to help. Do not assume a relative can or wants to take on every task.
                                                                                • Write the location of your current legal documents and the professional or office to contact. Identify originals separately from copies.
                                                                                • List immediate responsibilities: dependent care, pets, essential household services, keys and any safety or access information that cannot wait.
                                                                                • Add the institutions where accounts and policies exist, using enough detail to identify them without exposing unnecessary credentials.
                                                                                • Date the page, choose a protected storage location and explain how the appropriate person can find it when needed.

                                                                                paragraphs
                                                                                heading
                                                                                Finding a document is not the same as being allowed to act
                                                                                paragraphs
                                                                                • Someone may know where an account is without being authorised to use it. A person named in a will may still need to follow the appropriate estate process. A person who helps with bills while you are well may not have the authority required if you lose capacity. Keep these questions separate from the practical question of where the paperwork lives.
                                                                                • For health-care preferences, [CaringInfo's state and territory resources](https://www.caringinfo.org/planning/advance-directives/) provide a starting point for the relevant advance-directive forms. Read the instructions for your location. An informal note about your wishes may help a conversation, but do not label it a legally effective directive without checking the requirements.
                                                                                • Use the [emergency contact and medical decision-maker guide](/guides/emergency-contact-and-medical-decision-maker) to distinguish being reachable from being authorised. If family circumstances, property ownership or legal arrangements are complicated, get professional advice before promising someone a role.

                                                                                A first version that is small enough to finish
                                                                                paragraphs
                                                                                • An invented example: Maya writes that the originals of her legal documents are with a named professional, the household folder is in the locked cabinet, and her sister knows the agreed access process. She lists the mortgage provider and insurer by name, not their passwords. She adds the contact for the person who can collect her child under the school's current arrangements.
                                                                                • That is not a complete estate or emergency plan. It is a starting point someone can follow. The next pass adds other institutions and responsibilities. The file distinguishes an agreed role from a person Maya still needs to ask, and it dates every section so a helper can spot older information.

                                                                                Check the file after a meaningful change
                                                                                items
                                                                                • Update contact details and document locations after a move, relationship change, new dependent or changed professional adviser.
                                                                                • Replace superseded directions clearly rather than leaving conflicting versions in several folders.
                                                                                • Review access after changing a lock, device, provider or security arrangement. Do not solve access by distributing credentials indiscriminately.
                                                                                • Ask the appropriate person whether the directions are understandable. They should be able to locate a named document without you giving a second set of instructions.
